title: G2.6 - Loop fault demonstrations and operational verification
intent: Formalize the four fault demonstrations (failure, retry, rejection, invalidation) on the live stack, gather orchestration-worker kill-restart recovery evidence, and add the governed repo-binding provisioning command, completing the G2 exit-gate verification.
scope: Prove the G2 exit gate: failures, retries, rejections and invalidation demonstrated on the live loop with inspectable evidence; a worker restart converges without human repair; repo bindings are provisionable through governance. The GitHub token-resolution design decision is surfaced to the Outcome Owner.
non_goals: Live GitHub PR creation against a real repository (deferred pending the credential-wiring decision)
Webhook ingestion, Runner Protocol extraction, or Execution Gateway work (G3)
Approve, merge, deploy, release, or create a ship record without independent review and explicit user acceptance
acceptance_criteria: Four fault demonstrations recorded on the live loop: failure (integration run failure -> claim refuted), retry (idempotent replay + stale-fence rejection), rejection (self-review/self-approve 403), invalidation (superseded submission -> derived invalid) — each with inspectable evidence on the live stack
Worker kill-restart recovery proven: killing the orchestration worker mid-loop leaves outbox events pending; restarting converges delivery and workflow state without human repair
Repo bindings provisionable through governance: a governed admin command creates the workspace repo binding with the receipt + audit pattern; the connector execute gate accepts it
Credential wiring decision surfaced: the design options for GitHub token resolution are documented for the Outcome Owner; no unilateral secret-transit decision

G2 exit gate verified: the signature-loop facts (target version, artifact revisions, criterion coverage, evidence, submission, review, acceptance, invalidation) render on the live stack with honest states
